key_insight: AlB₁₂–Al detonation coatings improved wear resistance over uncoated steel 45, with AB70 showing stable tribological performance across tested friction conditions.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer a potential route to improving the durability of steel components exposed to sliding wear.
method: Deposited AB70 (70 wt.% AlB₁₂, 30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (30 wt.% AlB₁₂, 70 wt.% Al) using a DNEPR-5M detonation-spray system.
Characterized coating thickness, hardness and friction-surface structure.
Evaluated friction and wear under varied sliding speeds and loads against uncoated steel 45.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coating thicknesses of approximately 170–200 μm and AB70 friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38 with wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km; oxidative and adhesive-abrasive wear mechanisms were identified.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test loads, sliding speeds or statistical variability, limiting extrapolation to service conditions.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
